lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo (photos/442158_1.jpg). Two-part cabinet: moulded cornice with rounded front corners, pair of arched glazed doors with lock to right door, four shelves behind; projecting fall-front secretaire drawer with flame-figured mahogany-type veneer, crossbanded surround, central escutcheon and two pierced pressed-brass bail handles (style may be later replacements); lower pair of arched raised-panel doors in figured timber, carved scroll corbels each side, plinth base. Colour and figure are consistent with Australian red cedar carcase with mahogany-faced drawer, matching the title. Glass looks old (wavy reflections). No secretaire interior shown.
lots.condition: Looks sound and presentable from the front: finish even, no obvious veneer losses, glass intact. Minor marks only visible at the plinth. Interior fittings, leather, back boards, and whether top and base are an original pair are all unseen.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please open the secretaire drawer: are all 8 small drawers and the pigeon holes present and original, and is the writing surface leather intact? Are the top and base an original pair (matching timber and backboards), are both keys working in all locks, is the glass original and uncracked, and are there any splits, veneer lifting, worm or replaced handles? Can the two sections be separated for pickup?

lots.key_photo_findings: One photo (photos/442698_1.jpg). Two tall slabs leaning against corrugated iron, each chalked '1118 9/10/26' with a 1118 sticker. Bright buttery yellow with fine, straight, even grain, consistent with Huon pine; no birdseye, burl or ripple figure seen. Each has a wide bark and sapwood edge on one side, so the clear usable width tapers from roughly 200 mm near the base to about 100 mm at the top. Using the corrugation pitch (about 76 mm) as a scale, each slab looks about 1.6 to 1.9 m long and up to about 200 mm wide, which is shorter than the researcher's 2.3 m estimate. Thickness not visible. Surfaces look rough sawn; a few small knots and minor end checking.
lots.condition: Rough sawn, bark-edged, narrow; dryness unknown. Small knots and some checking; no obvious large splits.
lots.question_for_gowans: What are the length, width and thickness of each slab? Are they air dried or recently milled, and is the timber confirmed as Huon pine (it has a distinctive oily, peppery smell when cut)? Any splits or borer in the sapwood edge?
